# [`std::chrono`](Stdlib-Chrono)

Module file: `stdlib/std/chrono.mla`

Checked integral durations with explicit runtime units, inspired by C++20
[`std::chrono::duration`](Stdlib-Chrono). Mlang currently uses a `Duration { count, unit }`
value instead of a compile-time period parameter. Supported units range from
nanoseconds through weeks.

[`std::chrono`](Stdlib-Chrono) also exposes Mlang's checked C++20 civil-calendar types and
operations (`year`, `month`, `day`, `weekday`, `year_month`,
`year_month_day`, and the month/day/weekday recurrence types). Their underlying
implementations remain shared with [`std::date`](Stdlib-Date); timezone and wall-clock
formatting APIs continue to live there.

```rust
mod std::chrono;
use std::chrono::Duration;
use std::chrono::DurationUnit;
use std::chrono::make_duration;
use std::chrono::duration_cast;
use std::chrono::duration_floor;
use std::chrono::duration_ceil;
use std::chrono::duration_round;
use std::chrono::duration_add;
use std::chrono::duration_compare;
use std::chrono::ClockKind;
use std::chrono::make_time_point;
use std::chrono::time_point_add;
use std::chrono::time_point_difference;
use std::chrono::time_point_round;
use std::chrono::HhMmSs;
use std::chrono::make_hh_mm_ss;
use std::chrono::format_hh_mm_ss;
use std::chrono::make12;
use std::chrono::make24;

let elapsed = make_duration(90, DurationUnit::Second).unwrap();
let milliseconds: Duration =
    duration_cast(elapsed, DurationUnit::Millisecond).unwrap();
let total: Duration = duration_add(
    elapsed, make_duration(2, DurationUnit::Minute).unwrap(),
    DurationUnit::Second).unwrap(); // 210 seconds
let order = duration_compare(elapsed, total).unwrap(); // Less
let rounded_minutes: Duration =
    duration_round(elapsed, DurationUnit::Minute).unwrap(); // 2 minutes
let start = make_time_point(elapsed, ClockKind::Steady).unwrap();
let later = time_point_add(
    start, make_duration(5, DurationUnit::Second).unwrap()).unwrap();
let elapsed_between: Duration = time_point_difference(
    later, start, DurationUnit::Second).unwrap(); // 5 seconds
let rounded_start = time_point_round(start, DurationUnit::Second).unwrap();
let clock_fields: HhMmSs = make_hh_mm_ss(elapsed).unwrap();
let formatted_time: str8 = format_hh_mm_ss(elapsed).unwrap(); // 00:01:30
let evening_hour: i32 = make24(7, true).unwrap(); // 19

let y = make_year(2024).unwrap();
let m = make_month(2).unwrap();
let d = make_day(29).unwrap();
let leap_day = make_year_month_day(y, m, d).unwrap();
let epoch_days = to_sys_days(1970, 1, 1).unwrap(); // 0
let epoch = from_sys_days(epoch_days).unwrap();
let epoch_point: sys_days = to_sys_days(epoch).unwrap();
let tomorrow = sys_days_add_days(epoch_point, 1).unwrap();
```

- Calendar constructors such as `make_year`, `make_month`, `make_day`,
  `make_year_month`, and `make_year_month_day` return [`option`](Quick-Guide#types) so invalid
  values are handled explicitly. Calendar arithmetic and conversion helpers
  include `year_is_leap`, `month_days`, `to_sys_days`, and `from_sys_days`.
- Recurring dates are available through `make_month_day` /
  `resolve_month_day`, `make_month_day_last` /
  `resolve_month_day_last`, `make_year_month_day_last`, and the numbered or
  final weekday helpers `make_year_month_weekday` and
  `make_year_month_weekday_last` with their corresponding `resolve_` forms.
- `make_weekday`, `weekday_c_encoding`, `weekday_iso_encoding`,
  `weekday_from_sys_days`, `weekday_of`, and `add_weekdays` cover typed weekday
  construction, conversion, and modular arithmetic.
- `sys_days` is a distinct system-clock day-precision time point storing its
  signed day count from the Unix epoch. `make_sys_days` and the
  `to_sys_days(year_month_day)` overload construct it; `from_sys_days(sys_days)`
  converts back. Day addition, subtraction, difference, and comparison use
  `sys_days_add_days`, `sys_days_subtract_days`, `sys_days_difference`, and
  `sys_days_compare`, with arithmetic overflow reported as `None`. The existing
  integer overloads remain available for compatibility.

- `make_duration(count, unit)` constructs a value for one of the declared
  `DurationUnit` alternatives.
- `duration_cast(value, unit)` converts to the requested unit. Conversions to
  coarser units truncate toward zero, like integral C++ `duration_cast`;
  conversions that overflow [`i64`](Quick-Guide#types) return `None`.
- `duration_floor(value, unit)`, `duration_ceil(value, unit)`, and
  `duration_round(value, unit)` provide C++ chrono rounding. `floor` and
  `ceil` handle negative fractions toward negative and positive infinity,
  respectively; `round` selects the nearest count and sends exact ties to the
  even count. Unrepresentable conversions return `None`.
- `duration_add(left, right, unit)` and `duration_subtract(left, right, unit)`
  convert both operands to the requested unit before checked arithmetic. A
  conversion or arithmetic overflow returns `None`.
- `duration_compare(left, right)` returns `Some(DurationOrder::Less)`,
  `Some(DurationOrder::Equivalent)`, or `Some(DurationOrder::Greater)` for
  exact cross-unit ordering. It avoids multiplying
  full counts by conversion factors, so even extreme [`i64`](Quick-Guide#types) values can be
  compared without overflow.

`DurationUnit` contains `Nanosecond`, `Microsecond`, `Millisecond`, `Second`,
`Minute`, `Hour`, `Day`, and `Week`. The module deliberately reports overflow
through [`option`](Quick-Guide#types) rather than wrapping counts.

`TimePoint` pairs a since-epoch `Duration` with `ClockKind::Steady` or
`ClockKind::System`, following C++20 [`std::chrono::time_point`](Stdlib-Chrono). Use
`make_time_point` for checked construction, `time_since_epoch` to inspect the
stored duration, and `time_point_add` / `time_point_subtract` for checked
arithmetic. Arithmetic chooses the finer of the point and offset units and
returns `None` when conversion or arithmetic overflows. `time_point_difference`
and `time_point_compare` reject different clock kinds because their epochs
cannot be compared. `steady_now()` returns a monotonic nanosecond point;
`system_now()` returns the system-clock Unix time at whole-second resolution.
`time_point_cast`, `time_point_floor`, `time_point_ceil`, and
`time_point_round` convert or round the since-epoch duration while retaining
the original clock identity. Their checked integral rounding follows the
corresponding C++20 chrono operations.

`make_hh_mm_ss(duration)` decomposes an integral duration into a separate sign,
non-negative total hours, minute and second fields in `0..60`, and a
non-negative fractional remainder expressed in the source unit. This follows
C++20 [`std::chrono::hh_mm_ss`](Stdlib-Chrono) decomposition while retaining Mlang's runtime
duration precision. It returns `None` if the absolute total hours cannot fit
in [`i64`](Quick-Guide#types).
`format_hh_mm_ss(duration)` returns the corresponding signed
`HH:MM:SS[.fraction]` string. Fractional digits retain the source resolution
(3 for milliseconds, 6 for microseconds, and 9 for nanoseconds); invalid or
unrepresentable values return `None`.

The 12/24-hour helpers `is_am(hour)`, `is_pm(hour)`, `make12(hour)`, and
`make24(hour, pm)` follow C++20 chrono conventions. The conversions return
`None` for out-of-range inputs; `make12` accepts `0..23`, while `make24`
accepts `1..12` and an AM/PM flag.
